message.content: {"912_8353802117637": {"answer": "B", "reason": "The chest radiograph demonstrates large, thin-walled cystic cavities with air-fluid levels located in the left lower lobe, which is the classic radiographic presentation of intralobar pulmonary sequestration."}, "912_8353802159336": {"answer": "B", "reason": "Intralobar sequestrations are predominantly found in the left lower lobe and are characterized by cystic changes with fluid levels due to recurrent infections, supplied by systemic arteries from the aorta."}, "912_8353802160047": {"answer": "B", "reason": "The presence of sharply demarcated, thin-walled cavities containing fluid levels in the left lower lobe is highly specific for intralobar pulmonary sequestration, distinguishing it from other cavitary lung diseases."}, "912_8353802196305": {"answer": "B", "reason": "The imaging findings of large thin-walled cavities with fluid levels in the left lower lobe, combined with a history of recurrent infections, are indicative of intralobar pulmonary sequestration."}}
